mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both stop falling and turn up, commuting density expands weekday foot traffic and lifts retail and recreation within four weeks. The mechanism is stronger when RESIDENTIAL is flat or easing, because people are spending more time outside home rather than substituting into home-based activity.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior four weeks even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each increase for at least two consecutive weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: A recent decline in PARKS mobility below its prior three-week level signals a shift away from discretionary outdoor outings toward indoor errands and shopping, which should raise RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks. The effect is fastest when GROCERY_PHARM is also stable, indicating the change is not just substitution into essential trips.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below the average of the previous 3 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 14 days after PARKS drops below its three-week moving average.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT drops sharply week over week, the same shock should reduce incidental shopping trips and lower RETAIL_REC within one week. This predicts a near-immediate negative co-movement because reduced station usage signals fewer discretionary trips into retail corridors.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases during the week after TRANSIT falls by more than 20 points week over week.

mechanism_narrative: In a stable weather-normal season, a sustained increase in PARKS mobility over two weeks competes with retail trips and pulls retail and recreation down over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails when park use rises because of a citywide reopening wave that also lifts all other out-of-home categories.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite PARKS staying elevated above its recent average.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES remain deeply negative but RESIDENTIAL stays positive, commuters are not returning to downtown and home-centered routines dominate, keeping RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next four weeks. The effect is strongest when TRANSIT is also depressed, confirming weak in-person circulation rather than only remote-work substitution.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises relative to the prior four weeks while WORKPLACES stays near current lows and RESIDENTIAL remains elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM after several weeks of softness indicates renewed short-trip activity that spills over into nearby retail visits within two weeks. This should raise RETAIL_REC even if broader commuting measures do not move, because the mechanism relies on neighborhood errand bundling rather than downtown traffic.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM turns positive week-on-week after being negative for 2 straight weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve over the next 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM turns up from a two-week decline.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both strengthen while RESIDENTIAL softens, the city is moving into a commuting-heavy regime that should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The claim fails if transit and workplace gains occur without any reduction in residential stickiness, because that would imply no net increase in discretionary out-of-home time.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both increase for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior four-week mean within 28 days after simultaneous gains in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: During a mild-fall, outdoor-heavy regime, elevated PARKS mobility diverts leisure demand away from retail destinations and suppresses RETAIL_REC within one week. The signal is strongest when TRANSIT does not improve, because the negative retail effect then comes from destination choice rather than broader mobility expansion.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above its prior 2-week average
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases in the week after PARKS rises above its prior two-week average, especially if TRANSIT is unchanged or weaker.
